from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.styles import PatternFill, Font
from openpyxl.formatting.rule import FormulaRule
from copy import copy
from pathlib import Path
import math
import re

input_path = Path("/mnt/data/spreadsheet/CF_11072/1_CF_11072_input.xlsx")
output_path = Path("/mnt/data/outputs/CF_11072_0_f6de7d02/1_CF_11072_output.xlsx")

wb = load_workbook(input_path)
ws = wb["Sheet1"]

# Allowed edit range only
min_row, max_row = 3, 12
min_col, max_col = 5, 6  # E:F

green_fill = PatternFill(fill_type="solid", fgColor="92D050")
white_fill = PatternFill(fill_type=None)
green_font = Font(color="006100")

def is_number(v):
    return isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) and not math.isnan(v)

def row_label(r):
    return str(ws.cell(r, 5).value or "").strip()

def norm_option(label):
    s = label.lower()
    if "1" in s:
        return "Option 1"
    if "2" in s:
        return "Option 2"
    return label.strip() or "Unknown"

# Remove direct fills we may replace, but ONLY in the allowed range.
# Keep any other cell attributes intact.
for r in range(min_row, max_row + 1):
    for c in range(min_col, max_col + 1):
        ws.cell(r, c).fill = copy(white_fill)

winner_rows = []
wins = {"Option 1": 0, "Option 2": 0}

def mark_winner_row(r, option_label=None):
    """Apply visible green fill to E:F in a winning row, within allowed range."""
    if min_row <= r <= max_row:
        for c in range(min_col, max_col + 1):
            cell = ws.cell(r, c)
            cell.fill = copy(green_fill)
            cell.font = copy(cell.font)
            cell.font = Font(
                name=cell.font.name, sz=cell.font.sz, b=cell.font.b, i=cell.font.i,
                vertAlign=cell.font.vertAlign, underline=cell.font.underline,
                strike=cell.font.strike, color="006100"
            )
        winner_rows.append(r)
        opt = norm_option(option_label if option_label is not None else row_label(r))
        if opt in wins:
            wins[opt] += 1

# 1) Average example: E3:F4, target = 10; lower ABS(result-target) is better.
# Conditional formatting is applied only inside E3:F4.
if is_number(ws["F3"].value) and is_number(ws["F4"].value):
    ws.conditional_formatting.add(
        "E3:F4",
        FormulaRule(formula=['=ABS($F3-10)=MIN(ABS($F$3-10),ABS($F$4-10))'],
                    fill=green_fill, font=green_font)
    )
    d3 = abs(ws["F3"].value - 10)
    d4 = abs(ws["F4"].value - 10)
    if d3 <= d4:
        mark_winner_row(3, ws["E3"].value)
    else:
        mark_winner_row(4, ws["E4"].value)

# 2) Locate metric blocks in E:F within the allowed range.
# A block is a metric heading row followed by two Option rows with numeric results.
for header_row in range(min_row, max_row - 1):
    header_text = f"{ws.cell(header_row,5).value or ''} {ws.cell(header_row,6).value or ''}".strip().lower()
    r1, r2 = header_row + 1, header_row + 2
    if r2 > max_row:
        continue
    if not (is_number(ws.cell(r1,6).value) and is_number(ws.cell(r2,6).value)):
        continue
    if "option" not in row_label(r1).lower() or "option" not in row_label(r2).lower():
        continue
    
    # Avoid re-processing the average block headed outside the answer range.
    if r1 == 3 and r2 == 4:
        continue
    
    # %CV: lower is better.
    if "cv" in header_text:
        rng = f"E{r1}:F{r2}"
        ws.conditional_formatting.add(
            rng,
            FormulaRule(formula=[f'=$F{r1}=MIN($F${r1}:$F${r2})'],
                        fill=green_fill, font=green_font)
        )
        v1, v2 = ws.cell(r1,6).value, ws.cell(r2,6).value
        mark_winner_row(r1 if v1 <= v2 else r2, ws.cell(r1 if v1 <= v2 else r2, 5).value)
    
    # Ratio or similar "higher is better" metric.
    elif "ratio" in header_text:
        rng = f"E{r1}:F{r2}"
        ws.conditional_formatting.add(
            rng,
            FormulaRule(formula=[f'=$F{r1}=MAX($F${r1}:$F${r2})'],
                        fill=green_fill, font=green_font)
        )
        v1, v2 = ws.cell(r1,6).value, ws.cell(r2,6).value
        mark_winner_row(r1 if v1 >= v2 else r2, ws.cell(r1 if v1 >= v2 else r2, 5).value)

# 3) Bonus: count which option has more green/wins.
# Write the summary only into blank rows inside E3:F12.
empty_rows = [
    r for r in range(min_row, max_row + 1)
    if ws.cell(r,5).value in (None, "") and ws.cell(r,6).value in (None, "")
]
if empty_rows:
    r = empty_rows[0]
    ws.cell(r, 5).value = "Green count"
    ws.cell(r, 6).value = f"Option 1: {wins['Option 1']}; Option 2: {wins['Option 2']}"
    ws.cell(r, 5).font = Font(bold=True)
if len(empty_rows) >= 2:
    r = empty_rows[1]
    if wins["Option 1"] > wins["Option 2"]:
        better = "Option 1"
    elif wins["Option 2"] > wins["Option 1"]:
        better = "Option 2"
    else:
        better = "Tie"
    ws.cell(r, 5).value = "Better option"
    ws.cell(r, 6).value = better
    ws.cell(r, 5).font = Font(bold=True)

output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
wb.save(output_path)

# Verification: reopen and print E3:F12 values and direct fill colors
wb2 = load_workbook(output_path)
ws2 = wb2["Sheet1"]
print("Saved:", output_path)
for r in range(3, 13):
    e = ws2.cell(r,5)
    f = ws2.cell(r,6)
    print(r, e.value, f.value, "fills:", e.fill.fgColor.rgb, f.fill.fgColor.rgb)
print("Conditional formatting ranges:", [str(x) for x in ws2.conditional_formatting])
